Subject: MSA redline Qs — infringement liability allocation

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the updated MSA draft. Our legal team reviewed Section 8 (Liability) and we have a couple of questions on how Redwood wants to handle IP-related indemnities vs. the overall liability cap. Two items in particular:

1) Siloing of exposure — BrightLayer's GC is proposing that any liability for IP infringement be "siloed" to the specific product line or Order Form where the allegedly infringing deliverable was used (i.e., don't let an IP claim against a specific integration consume our global cap). Is Redwood open to language that limits IP indemnity exposure to the affected Order Form(s)?

2) Subrogation & insurance interplay — we expect our insurers to want explicit subrogation rights and to coordinate any recoveries; can Redwood confirm whether Redwood's indemnity / cap language would allow subrogation and not prejudice claim recoveries by insurers (we're attaching a suggested clause).

We attached a redline (BrightLayer_MSA_Redline_20270516.docx) with the suggested edits and an IP-claim-flow-diagram. Happy to jump on a short call if it's easier. We are trying to close commercial terms this week.

Best,

Team — looping you in. Evan's two asks are: (A) restrict IP indemnity exposure to the impacted Order Form(s) ("siloing"), and (B) confirm subrogation/insurance won't be impeded by our indemnity/cap wording.

Quick thoughts:
- Commercial: Aditya, siloing reduces enterprise risk exposure but may increase customer pushback if they want global insurance-based protections. If we accept siloing, what's the price impact for a dedicated Order Form carve?
- Legal: Karthik / Marissa, need contract language options: (1) full IP carveout from the monetary cap (classic carveout), (2) siloed cap limited to the revenue attributable to the affected Order Form (proportional allocation), or (3) a hybrid (cap remains but IP indemnities have a separate sub-cap). Also need to confirm subrogation language that preserves insurer rights but doesn't create third-party beneficiary issues.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik: can you draft 2 alternative redline snippets we can share (carveout vs. siloed allocation)?
- Marissa: confirm whether our current indemnity language already allows insurer subrogation or if we need an explicit line.
- Aditya: give rough commercial guidance on whether siloing needs a term/price adjustment.

Evan — we'll aim to send back redline options by EOD tomorrow. If you have constraints on wording (e.g., counsel must be able to pursue direct recovery), highlight them.

Thanks — Neha

Subject: RE: MSA redline Qs — infringement liability allocation (draft snippets)

Neha / team / Evan — attaching two short draft snippets below that we can insert into Section 8. I kept the language modular so commercial can pick an approach.

Option A — IP carveout (most Redwood-friendly):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Redwood's liability for claims alleging infringement of a third party's intellectual property arising from the Customer's use of the Services shall not be subject to the monetary limitation set forth in this Agreement. Redwood shall indemnify, defend and hold Customer harmless from and against any Losses arising from such claims, subject to the procedures in the Indemnity Section."

Option B — Siloed allocation (compromise):
"For claims solely relating to infringement of a third party's intellectual property, liability shall be allocated to the Order Form(s) under which the allegedly infringing Service or Deliverable was provided. The aggregate liability for such claims shall be capped at the total Fees paid or payable by Customer under the applicable Order Form(s) during the preceding twelve (12) month period, unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

Subrogation / Insurance carve-in language (to preserve insurer rights while avoiding third-party beneficiary issues):
"Each party's insurers shall have the right of subrogation; provided, however, that a party shall not exercise subrogation rights against the other party to the extent such exercise would reduce the indemnified party's recovery under this Agreement. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to confer any rights on insurers as third-party beneficiaries without the prior written consent of both parties."

Notes:
- Option A is cleaner for customers but increases Redwood's tail risk; reserve/escrow or insurance would be our mitigations.
- Option B aligns risk to specific purchases; sales and pricing should consider attaching an insurance/indemnity fee to Order Forms where customers insist on broader remedies.

I'll attach a redline snippet to the DocuSign link once we agree which option to propose.

-Karthik

Subject: RE: MSA redline Qs — infringement liability allocation — proposal

Evan — thanks for the patience. Based on legal and commercial input, Redwood proposes the following path forward to get to signature this week:

1) Default approach: Offer Option B (Siloed allocation) in the MSA. This limits IP indemnity exposure to Fees attributable to the impacted Order Form(s) over the prior 12 months. Rationale: balances BrightLayer's ask for allocation and Redwood's need to cap enterprise-wide exposure.

2) Optional add-on: If BrightLayer wants an IP carveout from the corporate cap (Option A), we can offer it as a purchasable add-on on the Order Form (one-time premium or higher per-seat rate) plus requirement that customer maintain commercial IP insurance with a minimum limit and name Redwood as a loss payee for claims covered by the add-on.

3) Subrogation: Redwood accepts the subrogation/insurance language proposed by Karthik (see below). We will not block insurer subrogation so long as it does not reduce BrightLayer's contractual recovery.

4) Logistics: We will upload a tracked redline with Option B inserted and the optional add-on language as a comment. Please review and let us know whether BrightLayer legal can accept Option B or prefers to purchase the add-on. If accepted, we'll route through our commercial DocuSign envelope (link below).

- BrightLayer: confirm preference by 2027-05-19 17:00 PT.
- Redwood (Neha / Aditya): pricing for optional add-on and insurance threshold by noon PT 2027-05-19.
- Karthik / Marissa: finalize redline for DocuSign and share link.
